CRITICAL (caught, not a crash): handleBookSearch does `setBookResults((res.books || res || []).slice(0,5))`. The actual response from GET /api/googlebooks/search is `{results, total_items, query_used, has_more, next_start_index}` (googlebooks_router.py:185-193) — there is no `books` field, so `res.books || res` evaluates to the whole response OBJECT, and `.slice()` throws TypeError. The throw is swallowed by the surrounding try/catch (`catch { setBookResults([]) }`), so the user just sees zero results for every search on this tour step — the 'add your first book' onboarding step is completely non-functional.
Should read `res.results` (matches SearchScreen.js and LibraryScreen's AddBookModal, which both correctly use `res.results`/`data.results`).

This is always undefined here (FeedScreen's equivalent shelf modal correctly falls back with `book.google_books_id || book.google_id`; AppTour does not), so books added from this step are saved with google_books_id=null, permanently breaking duplicate-detection for them.

`key={book.google_books_id}` on the result row (line 423) and `setAddingBook(book.google_books_id)` (line 194) both use the same always-undefined field, so every result row would share the same React key and the per-row 'adding' spinner (`addingBook === book.google_books_id`) would light up on ALL rows simultaneously while any one add is in flight.
